STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like strategy with forgiveness and endgame. The trace simulates matches against population slots (always-C, TFT, forgiving TFT variants) and considers modifying the parent to exploit unconditional cooperators by defecting when the opponent has never defected, while restoring cooperation against retaliatory opponents.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent starts C. Let's see against slot3" / "Parent starts C. I'll start C."
STRATEGY: The parent starts by cooperating, then defects to test whether the opponent retaliates, and cooperates once after its own defection to observe the response. The trace simulates this against TFT, pure C, slot3, slot8, and slot10, and revises the rule to switch to always-defect only when the opponent has never retaliated to any prior defection.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent is very cooperative, rarely defects. We can improve by adding more controlled exploitation." and "Parent fitness ~265. This could be around 300. So we should implement this."
STRATEGY: The parent is described as very cooperative and rarely defecting; the trace simulates a revised strategy that starts cooperative, tests with early defections, then defects repeatedly when no retaliation is observed, and cooperates to observe/restore after retaliation; changes include adding controlled exploitation, retaliation detection, and endgame defection.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "This seems like we might get stuck in a loop of D/D and C/D? Let's see pattern." / "We need to ensure the strategy doesn't get stuck in a low-scoring equilibrium."
STRATEGY: The parent is a hand-coded conditional strategy that cooperates initially, defects on the second round, exploits non-retaliatory opponents, and otherwise retaliates based on opponent defection counts and recent history. The trace manually simulates this strategy against several opponents (slot3, pure C, TFT, slot8) to estimate scores and detect punishment loops. It then proposes and tests modifications: adding a "cool-down" rule that cooperates when the parent has defected 4+ times in the last 10 rounds, and adjusting forgiveness thresholds, to break alternating low-scoring cycles.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: "My earlier simulation had us defecting more than twice, which triggered permanent punishment. But our strategy only defected twice before restoring!"; "The earlier simulation where we kept defecting was wrong because I mistakenly had non_ret true."; "Let's re-check my simulation: at r5, I said non_ret true. That was a mistake!"
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the strategy is fine!"; "So the strategy seems robust. Let's finalize the code."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates first, defects on round 3, then uses non-retaliatory detection, a recent-defection cool-down, and opponent-defection thresholds to decide. Simulated against slot8 (a conditional punisher) and slot3. Changed by correcting the r5 non_ret misread, adding an 80% opponent-defection rule, and adding a final-round defect at n==99.
